title: Minimum Jumps to Reach Home
summary: A bug starts at position 0 and aims to reach position x on the x-axis.
statement: A bug starts at position 0 and aims to reach position x on the x-axis. It can jump forward by exactly a positions or backward by exactly b positions, but cannot jump backward consecutively or to forbidden positions. The bug cannot jump to negative positions. Given forbidden positions and a, b, x, determine the minimum jumps needed to reach x, or return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: Positions are nonnegative; forbidden positions cannot be visited.
Jump forward by a or backward by b, but never backward twice consecutively. Return minimum jumps or -1.
hints: Position alone is insufficient state because the previous jump controls the next legal moves.
Breadth-first search pairs each position with whether the last move was backward.
Enqueue forward always and backward only after a non-backward move; skip forbidden, negative, repeated, and safely out-of-range states.
BFS explores legal sequences by length, so its first target state has minimum jumps.
